items.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016
items.q: So I was teaching Common piano lessons. I used to go to his house and give him piano lessons.

ctx.x: D’Angelo and Erykah Badu, but with people like Flying Lotus and Kendrick Lamar obviously and Chance the Rapper who are doing that a lot. And it’s becoming really big. What do you think is the cause of that at this time now in history, being such a big movement that’s happening right now?

Well I think there was two waves of it. I think there was one wave in the early or late 90s, the neo-soul movement. I was in New York when that happened. I didn’t realize it at the time but it was happening. I got to New York in ’97. I met Bilal in ’97. We started working with his album. And we were working on his album at Electric Lady Studios, Jimi Hendrix’s studio. And Erykah was on the — we were on the top floor, Erykah was on the middle floor and D’Angelo was on the bottom floor. So I literally watched…
